Let
\[
f(g)=7^{c(g)}\qquad(g\in A_6).
\]
The matrix is the matrix of right convolution by the central element
\[
z=\sum_{g\in A_6} f(g)g
\]
on the regular representation of \(A_6\). Hence if \(z\) acts on an irreducible \(A_6\)-module \(V\) of dimension \(d\) by the scalar \(\lambda_V\), then
\[
\det A=\prod_V \lambda_V^{d^2}.
\]

Now view \(z\) inside \(\mathbb C[S_6]\). Since
\[
\operatorname{sgn}(g)=(-1)^{6-c(g)},
\]
we have
\[
z=\frac12\sum_{g\in S_6}\bigl(7^{c(g)}+\operatorname{sgn}(g)7^{c(g)}\bigr)g
=\frac12\left(\Omega(7)+\Omega(-7)\right),
\]
where
\[
\Omega(x)=\sum_{g\in S_6}x^{c(g)}g.
\]

By the Jucys-Murphy identity,
\[
\Omega(x)=\prod_{k=1}^6\left(x+\sum_{i<k}(ik)\right),
\]
so on the Specht module \(S^\lambda\),
\[
\Omega(x)\text{ acts by }P_\lambda(x)=\prod_{(i,j)\in\lambda}(x+j-i).
\]
Thus \(z\) acts by
\[
\lambda_\lambda=\frac12\bigl(P_\lambda(7)+P_\lambda(-7)\bigr).
\]

The relevant \(S_6\)-partitions giving the \(A_6\)-irreducibles are
\[
(6),\ (5,1),\ (4,2),\ (4,1,1),\ (3,3),\ (3,2,1),
\]
with \(A_6\)-dimensions
\[
1,\ 5,\ 9,\ 10,\ 5,\ 8,8.
\]
For \((3,2,1)\), the \(16\)-dimensional \(S_6\)-module splits into two \(8\)-dimensional \(A_6\)-modules, and both receive the same scalar because \(z\) is constant on the split \(A_6\)-classes.

Computing the content products gives:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\lambda & \dim_{A_6} & \lambda_\lambda\\ \hline
(6) & 1 & 335160\\
(5,1) & 5 & 176400\\
(4,2) & 9 & 129360\\
(4,1,1) & 10 & 105840\\
(3,3) & 5 & 119952\\
(3,2,1) & 8,8 & 105840
\end{array}
\]
Therefore
\[
\det A
=
335160\cdot 176400^{25}\cdot 129360^{81}\cdot 105840^{100+64+64}\cdot 119952^{25}.
\]
So
\[
\det A
=
335160\cdot 176400^{25}\cdot 129360^{81}\cdot 105840^{228}\cdot 119952^{25}.
\]

Factoring,
\[
335160=2^3 3^2 5\,7^2\,19,
\]
\[
176400=2^4 3^2 5^2 7^2,\quad
129360=2^4 3\,5\,7^2\,11,
\]
\[
105840=2^4 3^3 5\,7^2,\quad
119952=2^4 3^2 7^2\,17.
\]
Combining exponents,
\[
\boxed{2^{1439}3^{867}5^{360}7^{720}11^{81}17^{25}19}.
\]
